name: DPRK-hosted animation subcontracting workflow

attribution.legal_posture: Specialist research attribution based on exposed work files; downstream commissioning-company knowledge or complicity remains unestablished.

caveats: Behavioral signals require corroboration and human review; staffing, badge, device, download, location, and sector signals become DPRK attribution only with supporting evidence.
medium-high for the exposed workflow; the reviewed evidence leaves downstream studios' knowing-hiring status unestablished.
Specialist research attribution based on exposed work files; downstream commissioning-company knowledge or complicity remains unresolved.

statements: 38 North reported that a misconfigured DPRK-hosted server was updated with animation work files and completed output apparently connected to international productions. Chinese-language instructions were consistent with intermediary subcontracting, and the researchers found no evidence that downstream commissioning companies knew DPRK labor was in the chain.
defensive_controls: Require subcontractor-chain disclosure and sanctions screening through every animation/visual-effects tier.
Contractually prohibit undisclosed offshore subcontracting and retain audit rights for source-file provenance.
Use work-file metadata, review comments, handoff timing and vendor payment paths to validate production provenance without assuming the named studios knew.
